claims.claim: #95 rescues the layout for a device that hears late that the time keeper changed
claims.quote: else if (early && isValidJoins(early, [...Object.keys(s.peers), id])) { s.joins = early; emit('layout'); }
claims.note: electLeader takes the layout kept in earlyLayouts from the new time keeper (line 46) and checks it again before using it. Layouts from other devices are kept at line 184. PR #95 (merged 2026-11-22, read through Qodo) describes the same change.

claims.claim: Join results (joined, retry, nomatch) are not rescued: they are still dropped in the same window by fromLeader, because the sender is not yet this device's time keeper
claims.quote: const fromLeader = (payload) => s.leader !== id && payload?.from === s.leader;
claims.note: Lines 198-200 call result() only when fromLeader passes. Nothing like earlyLayouts keeps results. The ticket's quote `payload.from !== s.leader` is not literal text on main: it is how PR #95's body describes the old layout check. The code says `payload?.from === s.leader` inside fromLeader, which means the same thing.

claims.quote: emit('nomatch', { dev: id, t: p.t, timedOut: true, latest: p.t === latest }); }, NO_MATCH_AFTER));
claims.note: Only result() clears the wait (line 168), and a dropped result never reaches result(), so the timeout fires after NO_MATCH_AFTER (line 119).

claims.claim: Results from a device that is not the time keeper are dropped today (acceptance point 2 says this must stay true)
claims.note: The same fromLeader check guards joined (198) and nomatch (200).

claims.claim: Kept layouts have a "sender must be in the room" check (`Object.hasOwn(s.peers, payload.from)`) and deleting it breaks no test
claims.quote: if (typeof payload.from === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(s.peers, payload.from) && payload.from !== id) earlyLayouts.set(payload.from, payload.joins);
claims.note: The check exists (holds). That no test breaks without it can't be run here. Static reading supports it: every layout the tests in tests/net.test.mjs send comes from a device in the room (B at 262, A at 281, L at 303).

claims.claim: "The new time keeper leaves straight away" has a browser test only, no unit test
claims.quote: the new time keeper leaves straight away: C takes over
claims.note: The words "straight away" don't appear in tests/net.test.mjs. Its only two-device leave (line 271, `leaves(devs, 'L', 'A')`) is the Rule 1 test, where both leave together, not the new time keeper leaving after taking over.

claims.claim: A kept layout can be out of date for a moment before the new time keeper's own layout replaces it (Low, not reproduced)
claims.note: The code does use the kept layout straight away. Whether it can be stale has not been reproduced.

questions: Should join results be kept per device the way earlyLayouts keeps layouts, then used when electLeader makes that device the time keeper? Or should the wait be left alone until the change is heard? How many results per device, and for how long (Rule 3 wants a named constant)?

If the late device's own NO_MATCH_AFTER timeout has already fired and shown "No match" before it hears of the change, should a kept "Joined" still be shown afterwards? Acceptance says 'whatever order', which seems to cover this.

A kept joined result has to be checked again at election time, as kept layouts are (isValidJoins against who is here now). Should retry and nomatch be checked again too, and should they still count if the push they answer is no longer this device's latest?

The old time keeper's results can arrive late, after the new one has taken over (the case Qodo raised on #95 for layouts). Should those be dropped, or should they clear kept results the way a layout from the current time keeper clears earlyLayouts (line 180)?
Should the repro in evidence/day-09/repro-pr95 become an asserting unit test in tests/net.test.mjs (it only logs now)?
